taxonomy.differentiation_note: US banks earn on a USD curve and a US credit cycle (card delinquency, commercial real estate) that eu_retail_banking does not carry, and the Fed and the ECB are on different paths. The vehicle (iShares S&P U.S. Banks, 39 holdings) is large money-centre and super-regional banks, so it also carries capital-markets and trading income, not only retail margins. It is not the regional-bank exposure (KRE/KBE) the original retirement named.

cycle_position.assessment: Mid-cycle on margins with a deposit-competition headwind.
cycle_position.rationale: FDIC industry NIM 3.32% in Q2 2026 (+6bp YoY) and JPMorgan raised 2026 NII guidance to $106.2B on 2026-10-13, but Citi (NIM ~2.46%) and Wells Fargo (~2.41%) guided Q3 margins down as higher Treasury yields forced deposit repricing. The sector ETF is 9.4% below its 52-week high with a 3-month return of -7.7% (2026-10-17).

key_metrics_to_monitor.comment: Q2 2026; Q3 report due Nov/Dec. Two consecutive declines is deact_03 of struct_higher_rates_bank_margins.
Raised from 105.5. Q4 guide 28.0; 2027 NII ex-markets 107.

risks: Deposit competition: rising Treasury yields pull deposits to higher-yielding alternatives, forcing banks to pay up; Citi and Wells Fargo guided Q3 margins down.
Fed path: another hike in October/December supports asset yields but slows loan demand and lifts credit costs.
Credit quality: card delinquency and commercial real estate exposure are the sector's named demand-side weak points.
Vehicle concentration: 39 holdings, money-centre heavy; trading and capital-markets income is part of the return.
Venue: IUS2.DE is broker_access assumed until confirmed in the broker app.
narrative_notes: Strategist reports (State Street, Goldman, Morgan Stanley) rate financials positive on loan growth and capital-markets activity, so the sector is widely recommended, but the ETF itself is down 7.7% over three months, so the narrative is not crowded in price.
